summary: Code-level verification of the implemented Michael Tier-2 checkpoint-send verb at EXEC-TO-PLAN. 149/149 tests pass across 7 files (runner artifact .artifacts/testing-exec/checkpoint-send-results.json, sha256 9053d75cc605be1fc26216b3d9a04d8778cfe333b4a6754a24f2c8d984c2b95e). FR-1..FR-9 are implemented substantially as the PRD promises and the RECIPIENT_SHA256 empty-string fail-closed mechanism is sound by construction. One HIGH finding: the new DDL test is not registered in the drive-reports-ddl.yml literal paths filter, so the ONLY instrument proving FR-7 AC-2 and FR-5 AC-4 never runs in CI. Three MEDIUM and five LOW findings recorded.
critical_issues: H1 (HIGH, FR-7 AC-2 / FR-5 AC-4): tests/ddl/michael-checkpoint-send-ddl.db.test.js and database/migrations/20260914_michael_checkpoint_send.sql are NOT in the paths filter of .github/workflows/drive-reports-ddl.yml. That filter is literal and per-file; every prior michael DDL pair IS registered (lines 127-129 for 20260906_michael_tables, lines 133-135 for 20260907_michael_v1_1_tables), and the workflow repeats the warning verbatim at least 8 times: 'this workflow's own paths filter is literal, so a PR touching only this SD's migration and its ddl test would otherwise trigger nothing'. This PR touches only the new pair, so the workflow will not fire. The job runs 'npx vitest run --config vitest.ddl.config.mjs' (line ~55) whose include is tests/ddl/**/*.db.test.js, so the test WOULD run once triggered - the gap is purely the trigger. Net effect: FR-7 AC-2 (at the ephemeral-PG DDL tier, a concurrent double-insert independently rejected by the DB constraint) and FR-5 AC-4 (proven at the ephemeral-PG DDL tier that the table RLS/REVOKE grants match the michael_* convention) have a correct instrument that is dead by construction. The DDL test file itself also documents at lines 19-22 that it collects ZERO tests from inside a .worktrees checkout, so it cannot be run here either. FIX: add the two paths to the workflow paths list, following the existing per-SD comment convention.
warnings: M1 (MEDIUM, FR-1/FR-6/FR-7): a staged-but-unfinalized ledger row is an UNCOUNTED SEND, contradicting the code's own claim. scripts/michael/checkpoint-send.mjs:163-165 stages outcome=refused / refusal_code=SEND_IN_PROGRESS before the external call, but the cap read at :124 filters .eq('outcome','sent') and the per-slot dedup at :136 reads that same array. A SEND_IN_PROGRESS row therefore counts for neither. If the process dies, or the finalize UPDATE fails, after Twilio accepted the message, the next in-window fire (each 15-min window catches two fires at :00 and :15) sees 0 sent, passes both the cap and the dedup, and sends a SECOND SMS; the DB partial unique index does not help because the second attempt's own finalize UPDATE to sent finds no conflicting sent row. Worst case: up to 8 chairman texts/day while the ledger reports 4 or fewer sent. The comment at :161-162 asserts the opposite ('never lets an uncounted send defeat FR-1's cap') - the audit trail exists but no reader counts it. Realistic trigger: lib/messaging/providers/twilio-provider.js:106 awaits fetch() unguarded, so a socket reset after Twilio processed the request throws straight out through runCheckpointSend. FIX: include staged rows in the cap and dedup reads (e.g. outcome=sent OR refusal_code=SEND_IN_PROGRESS), or stage under a distinct outcome those reads count.

M1b (MEDIUM, sub-point of M1): the finalize-failure branch at checkpoint-send.mjs:181-186 attributes the failure solely to a lost unique-index race, but writeRows (lib/michael/db.mjs:65-79) returns ok:false for ANY error, and the .select('id').single() shape also errors when zero rows match. The code cannot distinguish 23505 from a transient DB failure, even though db.mjs:70-72 passes error.code through expressly for that purpose and lib/michael/feeder.mjs:127 already exports isUniqueViolation() for it. The refusal code is a generic LEDGER_FINALIZE_FAILED, so the operator cannot tell 'another process sent it' from 'we sent it and lost the record'.

M2 (MEDIUM, FR-4 AC-2 coverage gap): the readProducingFeederCounts -> summarizeCounts -> composeCheckpointBody wiring is never tested end-to-end. Every runCheckpointSend test seeds fakeSb with only michael_checkpoint_send_enabled (checkpoint-send.test.js:45 ENABLED_ROW), so the michael_feeder_runs read returns [] and the body is always 'no counts available (as-of unavailable)'; the TS-9 success assertion at :202 only checks stringContaining('Michael checkpoint:'). FR-4 AC-2 (a test asserts the composed body reflects the actual producing run's as-of value, not the checkpoint's own send time) is therefore satisfied only at the pure-helper tier (:57-66), not for the verb. I manually verified the column names ARE correct (feeder, et_date, attempt, counts, finished_at all exist per database/migrations/20260906_michael_tables.sql:151-167), so this is not currently broken - but nothing in the suite would catch a rename, and a silently-empty read degrades to a permanently content-free checkpoint.

M3 (MEDIUM, FR-3 AC-2 coverage gap): lib/michael/checkpoint-identity.mjs has NO test file anywhere in the diff. FR-3 AC-2 names the module explicitly: 'A partial identity (any 1 or 2 of the 3 MICHAEL_TWILIO_* vars set) resolves to null from checkpoint-identity.mjs'. The provider-side half is proven very well (tests/unit/messaging/twilio-provider-identity.test.js:65-85, genuinely non-vacuous - it stubs fetch so shouldRefuseRealSend does not short-circuit, and asserts the real Twilio URL and auth header were built), and the verb-side half is covered by injecting resolveIdentity returning null (checkpoint-send.test.js:239). But the actual resolver is never executed by any test, so its three env var NAMES (MICHAEL_TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID / _AUTH_TOKEN / _MESSAGING_SERVICE) are never asserted. A typo in one would make the verb permanently refuse IDENTITY_UNCONFIGURED with a fully green suite.

L1 (LOW): --now-minute is dead code. checkpoint-send.mjs:96 tests typeof a['now-minute'] === 'number', but parseArgs (lib/michael/db.mjs:97-120) only ever yields strings or boolean true, so the branch is unreachable from any argv. It reads as a testability seam but cannot activate; the tests correctly use the now injection instead.

L2 (LOW, observability): nothing in scripts/, lib/, api/ or tests/ reads michael_checkpoint_send_ledger or michael_checkpoint_send_enabled other than the verb itself. With RECIPIENT_SHA256 shipped empty, production will write a refused/RECIPIENT_HASH_MISMATCH row 8x/day indefinitely and no gauge, brief, or check surfaces it. FR-10 explicitly scopes out MISSED-window reconciliation, which is a different thing from a verb that is permanently refusing every window - that state is currently undetectable except by manual query.

L3 (LOW, DDL instrument): tests/ddl/michael-checkpoint-send-ddl.db.test.js:153-167 proves the partial unique index via INSERT-vs-INSERT, but the application path that actually depends on it is an UPDATE into conflict (checkpoint-send.mjs:178-180). Same index, so the behaviour follows, but the instrument does not cover the transition the code reasons about at :181-186. The test is otherwise strong - notably :175-180 proves the verify block can go RED, which is a real anti-vacuity control.

L4 (LOW, FR-4 fidelity): summarizeCounts (checkpoint-send.mjs:56) selects the FIRST numeric entry via Object.entries(row.counts).find(...). counts is JSONB, and Postgres does not preserve insertion order (it orders object keys by length then bytewise), so which number reaches the chairman is decided by JSONB key ordering rather than intent. The test at :57-66 passes JS object literals, which DO preserve insertion order, so it proves an ordering production will not reproduce. Compounding it, the template emits a bare unlabelled number ('calendar-read:3' - 3 of what?), so an arbitrary key selection is not even visible as wrong.

L5 (LOW, contract accuracy): runCheckpointSend JSDoc says 'Never throws' (checkpoint-send.mjs:84), but sendFn is awaited unguarded at :171 and lib/messaging/providers/twilio-provider.js:106 awaits fetch() with no try/catch, so a network-layer throw propagates. main() catches it at :199, but the documented contract of the injectable seam is not enforced.
recommendations: Before merge: register database/migrations/20260914_michael_checkpoint_send.sql and tests/ddl/michael-checkpoint-send-ddl.db.test.js in the paths filter of .github/workflows/drive-reports-ddl.yml, following the per-SD comment convention already used at lines 125-135. This is the whole of H1 and is a 4-line change.

Verify the DDL test green from the MAIN checkout post-merge, never from this worktree - the file's own header at lines 19-22 states it collects ZERO tests under .worktrees, so a bare exit-0 from here would be a false pass.

M1: make the cap and dedup reads count staged rows, so an interrupted send cannot be re-sent by the next fire in the same window. Either widen the reads to include refusal_code=SEND_IN_PROGRESS or stage under a distinct outcome value.
M1b: import isUniqueViolation from lib/michael/feeder.mjs and branch the finalize-failure path on it, so a lost race and a transient DB failure get distinct refusal codes.

M2: add one runCheckpointSend test that seeds michael_feeder_runs rows in fakeSb and asserts the composed body carries the producing run's finished_at - this closes FR-4 AC-2 at the verb tier and pins the column names.
M3: add lib/michael/checkpoint-identity.test.js exercising all 8 env-var subsets, which is the literal instrument FR-3 AC-2 names.
L1: delete the unreachable --now-minute branch at checkpoint-send.mjs:96, or make parseArgs coerce it, rather than leaving a seam that reads as live.
L4: name the count key in the body template (e.g. 'calendar-read events:3') and select the key explicitly per feeder rather than relying on JSONB ordering.

metadata.ddl_tier_skip_reason: No local Postgres/docker available, and vitest.ddl.config.mjs collects zero files from inside a .worktrees checkout (documented at tests/ddl/michael-checkpoint-send-ddl.db.test.js:19-22). Reviewed statically against the migration SQL instead.
